goals.0: Telling long and short vowels apart
goals.2: Saying w, v, z, j, sch, ch correctly
grammar.0.title: Vowels: long and short
grammar.0.intro: A vowel is long before one consonant (Name) and short before two (Mann). Tap to listen.
grammar.0.note: For ö and ü change your lips: ö = round lips + “e”, ü = round lips + “ee”.
grammar.1.title: Double vowels
grammar.1.intro: ei and ie read the opposite way round! ei = “eye”, ie = long “ee”.
grammar.2.title: Consonants that differ from English / Bangla
grammar.2.intro: w = “v”, v = “f”, z = “ts”, j = “y”, sch = “sh”, ch = a soft “h” — these six cause most mistakes.
grammar.3.title: Spelling and sound mostly match
grammar.3.text: Most German words are read exactly as they are written. At the end of a word, b, d, g sound like p, t, k (Tag → “tahk”). The German r is soft and in the throat, not rolled on the tongue like the Bangla r.
quiz.7.prompt: Put the words in order: “How do you say that?”
quiz.7.why: Question word first, then the verb.
